evidence.description: FIND-101 confirmed RESOLVED by direct Read + hand computation against evidence/fixtures/transit-plan-tokyo-shinjuku.json: best journey (earliest arrival=84309) has departureSecs=83280 → durationSecs=1029; leg.arrivalSecs=84180 so journey.arrivalSecs(84309)-leg.arrivalSecs(84180)=129=egressWalkSecs, proving durationSecs ALREADY includes egress. accessWalkSecs=61 is NOT yet included (departureSecs equals the leg's own departureSecs, not door-departure). durationSecs(1029)+access(61)=1090, matching transit.js:49's formula exactly and transit.test.js:29's updated assertion of 1090 (was 1219, the double-counted value). No re-add of egressWalkSecs remains in the code.

FIND-002 spot-check: still wired — makeRouteCache imported, cache.getOrCompute keyed on (uid,geo,geo,bucket) gates the compute closure, travel-transit-wire.test.js's 'repeated ticks... call the provider ONCE' test still exercises this path unchanged.
FIND-006 spot-check: still resolved — both previously-dead modules (money-path.js, route-cache.js) retain real non-test production importers (grep-confirmed).

FIND-103 confirmed RESOLVED: loadController wraps existsSync+JSON.parse+field-read in try/catch, falling back to a fresh RollbackController on any parse failure. money-path-monitor.test.mjs exercises exactly the 3 required cases (corrupt JSON → fresh controller no-throw, valid JSON → restored, missing file → fresh) — all 3 read and hand-verified logically consistent with loadController's implementation (default rc.consecutiveFail=0/incidentOpen=false/rollbackFired=false from the RollbackController constructor, per money-path.js:38-44).

The pre-existing 'picks EARLIEST ARRIVAL, not journeys[0]' synthetic test uses journey objects with no accessWalkSecs/egressWalkSecs fields; `Number(best.accessWalkSecs) || 0` correctly defaults to 0, so the FIND-101 fix does not regress this test (500+0=500, matches assertion) — hand-traced, no double-counting introduced for fixtures lacking walk fields.

FIND-102 confirmed RESOLVED to the standard the finding itself named: money-path-monitor.mjs now performs the SAME restore→sleep(20s)→re-run-liveOk pattern as netlify-deploy.yml's own flap guard (lines 91-98: restore, sleep 20, re-smoke, log FLAP GUARD if still failing) — hand-compared line-by-line, the two are structurally identical. Neither implementation pre-checks the candidate deploy's content before restoring (Netlify's API does not expose a way to probe a non-live deploy's served content without restoring it first); judged against the finding's own stated reference standard ('mirroring netlify-deploy.yml's approach'), this is met. The RollbackController's persisted one-restore-per-incident + one-alert-per-incident semantics (money-path.js:38-66, unchanged) mean a failed-restore's escalate=true IS surfaced in that incident's single Telegram alert (money-path-monitor.mjs:92) — hand-traced across 3 simulated ticks (fail→fail+rollback+unhealthy+alert→fail+no-op-by-design) and found consistent with the documented dedup/flap-guard invariant, not a new bug.
Synth-failure fallback re-confirmed unchanged and safe: playWakeClip's catch always calls openGeminiLive(); openGeminiLive is idempotent via `if (gemini) return;`; never a silent call.

Minor naming imprecision noted but not filed as a finding: transit.js:50 labels `inVehicleSecs: best.durationSecs` even though best.durationSecs includes the egress walk (per the FIND-101 analysis), so the field is not literally in-vehicle time. Grep-confirmed zero consumers of parsed.inVehicleSecs anywhere in apps/ — it is dead/unused output, so this is a documentation-accuracy nit with no behavioral impact, not a structural defect.

The `if (process.argv[1] && fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === process.argv[1])` run-only-when-main guard is the correct, standard ESM idiom — verified it lets money-path-monitor.test.mjs import loadController without triggering main()'s network calls (the test file only imports { loadController }, never invokes main), and does not affect direct `node money-path-monitor.mjs` invocation.

FIND-001 re-confirmed non-blocking per this iteration's charter: nixpacks.toml is syntactically correct (real nix packages, correct '...' preservation), the synth-failure fallback is proven safe independent of whether the config works on Railway, and execution-notes.md explicitly documents the remaining PROD PROOF step (re-run the real-call E2E against the deployed Railway service post-merge) as OUTSTANDING but not disk-verifiable — accepted as deferred per this review's own charter, not re-raised as a blocker.

FIND-001.note: Unchanged from iteration-4: disk-level fix (nixpacks.toml) verified correct; PROD PROOF remains a documented, required post-merge step (execution-notes.md:37-39), not re-litigated as a blocker per this iteration's explicit charter.

FIND-002.note: Spot-checked, still intact: route-cache.js wired into travel.js's directionsMinutes via cache.getOrCompute; travel-transit-wire.test.js's cache-hit test unchanged.

FIND-005.note: Spot-checked, still intact: geocodeAddress memoizes on module-level _geoMemo Map (travel.js:155,161), accepted deviation as documented.

FIND-006.note: Spot-checked, still intact: money-path.js and route-cache.js retain real production importers (grep-confirmed).

FIND-101.note: parseTransitPlan no longer double-counts egressWalkSecs: durationSecs = best.durationSecs (already includes egress, hand-proven from the fixture's own numbers) + accessWalkSecs only. transit.test.js:29 now asserts the correct 1090, not the buggy 1219.

FIND-102.note: money-path-monitor.mjs now re-runs liveOk() after the Netlify restore and logs/alerts a distinct 'FLAP GUARD: restored ... but site STILL failing' state when the rollback target is itself unhealthy — structurally identical to netlify-deploy.yml's own flap-guard pattern (the reference standard the original finding named), which also restores-then-reverifies rather than pre-checking.

FIND-103.note: loadController wraps the state-file read (existsSync + JSON.parse + field access) in try/catch, falling back to a fresh RollbackController on any corruption. money-path-monitor.test.mjs covers corrupt/valid/missing-file cases, hand-verified consistent with the implementation.

findings.issue: specs/behavioral-spec.md C6/OQ4 explicitly requires the 15-min monitor host to be a GitHub Actions SCHEDULED workflow (RESOLVED text, a MUST per this project's own no-optional-spec rule). The implementation instead targets OpenClaw cron (code comment cites a conflicting project rule), the spec was never updated to match, and this repo contains ZERO scheduled GHA workflow (.github/workflows/ has only the deploy-triggered netlify-deploy.yml) and no verifiable evidence the monitor is registered on any host — the OpenClaw cron config lives in a separate private repo outside this worktree. C5/C6's core 'continuous 15-min monitoring' guarantee is therefore unverifiable from disk and possibly not wired at all in production.
findings.fix: See findings/FIND-104.json for the two acceptable remediation paths (implement the spec'd GHA schedule workflow, OR update the spec + attach verifiable registration evidence for the OpenClaw alternative).
